Q5

#eval plot
ggplot(adults, aes(x = Religiosity_score, y = Lying)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = .0)

#filtered data
df5 <- adults %>% 
  mutate(
    dummy_lying = ifelse(Lying == "never", 1, 0)
  )

myGlm <- glm(dummy_lying ~ Religiosity_score, data = df5, family = binomial)
summary(myGlm) %>% pander()
  Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)
(Intercept) -4.279 0.63 -6.793 1.102e-11
Religiosity_score 0.02265 0.009948 2.276 0.02283

(Dispersion parameter for binomial family taken to be 1 )

Null deviance: 403.7 on 1007 degrees of freedom
Residual deviance: 398.4 on 1006 degrees of freedom 
#ANSWER: p-value = 0.02283  (or rounded = 0.023)

Q6

Wilcoxon test. I think it’s rank sum. I’m not sure.

boxplot(Religiosity_score ~ Dominant_hand, data = adults)

wilcox.test(Religiosity_score ~ Dominant_hand, data = adults)
## 
##  Wilcoxon rank sum test with continuity correction
## 
## data:  Religiosity_score by Dominant_hand
## W = 49934, p-value = 0.1307
## alternative hypothesis: true location shift is not equal to 0
#ANSWER: p-value = 0.1307

Q11

#new column
df11 <- adults %>% 
  mutate(
    dummy_only_child = ifelse(Only_child == "yes", 1, 0)
  )

#logistic regression model
myGlm <- glm(dummy_only_child ~ Number_of_siblings, data = df11, family=binomial)
summary(myGlm) %>% pander()
  Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)
(Intercept) 1.405 0.185 7.593 3.122e-14
Number_of_siblings -2.668 0.1962 -13.6 4.024e-42

(Dispersion parameter for binomial family taken to be 1 )

Null deviance: 1130 on 1001 degrees of freedom
Residual deviance: 765 on 1000 degrees of freedom 
#predict probability
predict(myGlm, newdata = data.frame(Number_of_siblings = 1), type="response")
##         1 
## 0.2204748
#plot
ggplot(df11, aes(x=dummy_only_child,y=Number_of_siblings))+
  geom_point()+
  # > This code below did this equation:
  # plot(Y ~ X, data=YourDataSet)
  # curve(exp(𝑏0+𝑏1*x)/(1 + exp( 𝑏0+𝑏1*x)), add = TRUE)
  # > "Just know, there is an equation actually graphing the line." - Bro. Saunders
  geom_smooth(method="glm", method.args = list(family="binomial"), se = FALSE)+
  theme_bw()+
  labs(
    title = "Siblings or Not",
    subtitle = "Logistic Regression"
  )+
  coord_flip()
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'
## Warning: Removed 8 rows containing non-finite outside the scale range
## (`stat_smooth()`).
## Warning: Failed to fit group -1.
## Caused by error:
## ! y values must be 0 <= y <= 1
## Warning: Removed 8 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range
## (`geom_point()`).

#ANSWER: 0.2204748  or 22% (around 30%)

Q23

Figure out which non-parametric test to run to get the correct p-value for this set of hypotheses:

\[ H_0 = \text{Each educational attainment is a sample from the same distribution of music diversity scores} \\ H_a = \text{At least one educational attainment has stochastically higher or lower music diversity scores} \]

I’m pretty sure it needs to be an ANOVA test.

myAov <- aov(Music_diversity_score ~ Education, data = adults)
summary(myAov)
##               Df Sum Sq Mean Sq F value Pr(>F)  
## Education      5    921   184.2    2.32 0.0415 *
## Residuals   1003  79640    79.4                 
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 1 observation deleted due to missingness
#ANSWER: p-value = 0.0415
